description:
At the October 27, 2026 Special Meeting for FY 26–27 Capital Projects, the Board of County Commissioners approved the purchase of 10 dump trucks from Truckworx. The cost is $220,000 per truck off the Sourcewell Contract # 032824-KTC.
The guaranteed auction value of our current fleet has reduced from the original guaranteed rate due to additional miles being placed on the dump trucks since the original rate was quoted; this decreased by $40,000. Additionally, the guaranteed auction value will be charged a 7% commission fee by JM Wood against the gross sale price. This means that if the trucks do not sell for more than the guaranteed rate, the BOCC would be obligated to an overall total of $676,660 between the buy and sale of the dump trucks this year, which is $166,660 more than the previously board-approved total of $510,000. Staff believes, after talking with the auctioneer that the trucks will bring more than the minimum guaranteed rate.
title: Request: Board approval to purchase dump trucks from Truckworx off Sourcewell contract - Jeffrey Register, Road and Bridge Director

description:
At the regularly scheduled meeting on October 13, 2026, the Board moved to set a public hearing for October 27th, 2026 at 6PM for the second reading and approval of this ordinance.
This item repeals the County's 1989 purchasing ordinance (Chapter 2, Article III, Division 2) and adopts a new Division 2, "Procurement." The new ordinance sets the legal framework for County purchasing, while the Purchasing Policy handles the day-to-day procedures. Dollar thresholds move out of the ordinance and into the Policy, where the Board can adjust them by vote instead of amending the Code. The update also adds federal procurement requirements for federally funded purchases, brings the local preference in line with state and federal law, and adds provisions the old code was missing, which include competitive proposals, emergency purchasing, cooperative purchasing, protest procedures, and ethics standards.
title: ADDITION: Request: Second reading and public hearing for an ordinance amending the Jackson County Code of Ordinances to repeal the existing Purchasing Ordinance to be replaced with an updated Procurement Ordinance. - Tyler Schaeffer, Procurement Officer

description:
Jackson County has been awarded $3.8 million through the Small Cities Community Development Block Grant Program, administered by the Florida Department of Commerce with funding provided by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The grant will support critical potable water infrastructure improvements, including construction of a new water production well near Interstate 10 and Highway 71, with an anticipated capacity of approximately 1,000 gallons per minute, and a new 180,000-gallon potable water storage tank near Highway 90 and Highway 71.
Adam Callaway, representing the Florida Department of Commerce, and State Representative Shane Abbott will join the Board for a ceremonial check presentation recognizing this investment in Jackson County's infrastructure and future economic growth.
The County wishes to recognize Representative Abbott, Senator Jay Trumbull, the Florida Department of Commerce, the County's legislative delegation, its governmental affairs representatives - including Alan Suskey and the Shumaker Advisors team - and the many other partners and advocates whose support helped make this grant award possible.
title: ADDITION: Presentation Recognizing a $3.8 Million CDBG Award for Potable Water Infrastructure Improvements

description: This item repeals the County's 1989 purchasing ordinance (Chapter 2, Article III, Division 2) and adopts a new Division 2, "Procurement." The new ordinance sets the legal framework for County purchasing, while the Purchasing Policy handles the day-to-day procedures. Dollar thresholds move out of the ordinance and into the Policy, where the Board can adjust them by vote instead of amending the Code. The update also adds federal procurement requirements for federally funded purchases, brings the local preference in line with state and federal law, and adds provisions the old code was missing, which include competitive proposals, emergency purchasing, cooperative purchasing, protest procedures, and ethics standards.
title:
Request: Set a public hearing for first reading and approval of changes to County Ordinance Chapter 2 Administration -

The Budget is balanced without the use of carryover funds, and by using revenue estimates for numbers that are not yet available from The Office of Economic and Demographic Research.

If the maximum millage rate of 8.2354 were chosen, this would require a 2/3 vote.
NOTE – REMINDER: Special Projects / Capital Projects Meeting: It is the plan of staff to have a special meeting near the end of September or early October to discuss the Special Projects List to identify Capital Purchases for the 2026/2027 Fiscal Year.

description: The equipment was purchased in July 2020 with CARES Act funds (grant funding) and a service agreement was also entered into at that time (not paid for by grant funding). The first year the fee for the maintenance agreement was $3200 and it has increased each year. The last year it was paid was in 2024 and it was in the amount of $ 3722.00. SOE Dunaway decided to not renew the maintenance contract due to the increasing cost. There were minor issues with the machine in 2024 and 2025. The technician was able to make some adjustments and repair the machine. However, in 2026 during the municipal elections it was discovered the machine needed major repairs. The repairs were going to approximately $3800. Supervisor Dunaway weighed options and decided to enter a lease for a new machine. There is a possibility that a neighboring Supervisor of Elections may be interested in purchasing our old machine as is. The request is to surplus the equipment, make an offering to the neighboring Supervisor of Elections and if not taken or if the Board prefers, surplus the equipment following normal protocol. description:
These additions are intended to support operational needs, reflect the true cost of service delivery, and ensure that the department can continue providing high‑quality public health services to our community.Below are the proposed new fees:
Page 3 under Child Health Services-Sports Physical and ECG
Florida Statute 1006.20 requires that all student-athletes complete a Preparticipation Physical Evaluation (PPE) using the Florida High School Athletic Association (FHSAA) EL2 form. Starting July 1st 2026 the statute mandates that this evaluation include a cardiovascular assessment to identify risk factors associated with sudden cardiac arrest in youth athletes.The FHSAA EL2 form, incorporated by reference into Florida law, includes a detailed cardiovascular history and physical examination. It also authorizes the evaluating provider to order an electrocardiogram (ECG).
The proposed Sports Physical ($50) and ECG ($20) fees reflect the staff time, clinical supplies, technology, and documentation required to comply with Florida law and ensure safe athletic participation.
Page 5 under Miscellaneous- Fingerprinting fees
The Health Department has increasingly been asked to provide fingerprinting services for individuals requiring background checks for employment, licensing, and volunteer work. These services require staff time, specialized equipment, and secure processing procedures. The proposed background fingerprinting ($100) and proposed background fingerprinting with photograph ($125) reflect the cost of providing these services while remaining accessible to residents.
title: Request: Board approval to add several new service fees to the County Health Department’s official fee schedule - Jana Barfield, MSN, RN, Administrator Florida Department of Health Jackson ​County

description:
This matter arises from an inverse condemnation action filed in 2017 concerning a property claim related to the County's Mt. Tabor Road project. As alleged in the complaint, the matter traces back to 2012, when the project was added to the County's work plan and the property owner was asked to execute a right-of-way deed. The complaint further alleges that project plans were approved in 2013, that a 2014 agenda item reflected that right-of-way deeds had been executed, and that the property owner later disputed that her property had been conveyed or taken with permission. The case has remained pending since that time, with the valuation of the property interest at issue being the remaining matter for resolution.
Approval of the proposed settlement will bring finality to litigation that has been pending for several years and will avoid the continued expenditure of County time, legal resources, and public funds associated with further proceedings. It will also eliminate the need for an upcoming trial on valuation and allow the County to conclude a long-running matter in a practical and fiscally responsible manner.
title: ADDITION: Request: Board Approval of Settlement Agreement- Real Estate Only - Clayton Knowles, County Attorney

description: The Commission may recall that the State denied the Corps the dredging permit in 2005, and they have not dredged the river since. The Riparian County Stakeholder Coalition's goal is to present a six-county perspective on how a navigation industry could exist and potentially increase economic development and recreational access to river resources while mitigating the dire impacts that were created while the Corps controlled the river. There are strategic ways that the Corps can improve navigation access without the wholesale detriment to the floodplain and bay, and our goal is not to deny dredging and navigation on the river but to urge the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to reject a return to full-scale dredging on the Apalachicola River. Gulf, Calhoun, Liberty and Gadsden County have already approved this resolution.
title:
Request: Board Approval of a Resolution urging a responsible approach to re-establishing navigation on the Apalachicola River without full-scale dredging -
Ken Jones, Riparian County Stakeholder Coalition

description:
Five leased motor graders have lease agreements expiring on February 4, 2026. Thompson Tractor, the County’s primary vendor for Caterpillar equipment, has offered to appraise the motor graders and provide a purchase offer. Previously, County Staff advised that allowing the leases to expire was the preferred option, as market research showed that reselling the equipment through a bid process would be risky and may not provide any return to the county.
However, based on our recent discussions with Thompson Tractor they have proposed to purchase the leased graders at a guaranteed price, there are 5 graders currently leased by the County from Caterpillar. This would require the County do a lease buyout from Caterpillar Financial Services Corp., and then immediately turn around and sell the graders to Thompson, based on their proposed agreed upon price, which removes any financial risk to the County. Additionally, the County would purchase one of the 5 graders, which would be paid for with; excess funds received from the Thompson Tractor sale, excess equipment sale proceeds, and the sale of existing old grader owned by Jackson County.
Staff requests approval of the proposed transaction, and technically authorizes:
* Exception to the procurement policy for the hours between the purchase from Caterpillar and the sale to Thompson Tractor
Additionally, staff is requesting to surplus and sell the current spare motor grader (unit 752) at Road and Bridge and replace it with one of the 140-13AWD serial number N9500419.

This project proposes the use of 11 different species of trees that are native to Florida and this region, estimating 300 new trees. Selected sections of this roadway are proposed where the COUNTY believes will be most aesthetically appealing and ecologically sustainable, and with consideration of driver safety in mind (i.e. clear zone, sight distance, etc.). Ground cover and filler trees may be considered and added as appropriate. All plants will be natural Florida Friendly. Project will require a one-year establishment by the contractor.

description:
At least every seven years, the county must determine if the need exists to amend the Comprehensive Plan to reflect changes since the last time the Comprehensive Plan was updated, pursuant to Rule Chapter 73C-49, Florida Administrative Code. Proposed changes were transmitted to Florida Commerce on October 29, 2024. The Objections, Recommendations, and Comments (ORC) Report was received from FloridaCommerce on December 27, 2024, with two comments; the final adoption hearing was held June 10, 2025, and the adopted document was submitted to FloridaCommerce.
A letter dated August 8, 2025, was received from James D. Stansbury, Chief, Bureau of Community Planning and Growth, stating the adopted document had been determined null and void ab initio due to an identified conflict with the application of Chapter 2025-190, Section 28, Laws of Florida (a/k/a Senate Bill 180). The identified conflict was to Chapter 4 Policy 2.1 of the ​Plan that had been updated to ​agree ​with Florida Administrative Code.
​Following discussions with FloridaCommerce, it was agreed that the County could re-adopt the ​Comprehensive Plan with a change to reset ​Chapter 4 Policy 2.1 to the wording of the previous version of the ​Plan.
title: Request: Second reading and adoption of a revision to the Jackson County Comprehensive Plan by Ordinance and approval of transmittal to Florida Department of Commerce — Kim Cole Sweazy, Community Development Director

description:
This item seeks Board determination that Jackson County residents have sufficient internet access to allow the County to publish legally required advertisements and public notices on its official website, as permitted under Florida Statute §50.0311.
Florida Statute §50.0311 allows governmental agencies to publish legal notices on a pubically accessible County website in lieu of newspaper publication, provided the agency determines that residents have adequate internet access. According to the 2023 U.S. Census data, 80.5% of Jackson County households have internet access, exceeding the 75% threshold set by Florida Statute §50.0311 for digital publication.
The County's website is publicly accessible and searchable at no cost. Legal notices must remain online for at least 90 days.
Once a year, the County will publish a notice in the printed newspaper that notifies citizens of the location of legal notices for the County, and instructs citizens on how to request copies of the notices. The County will maintain a registry of names, addresses, and e-mail addresses of property owners and residents who have requested in writing that they receive legally required advertisements and public notices from the County by first class mail or e-mail.
This request is in effort to reduce advertising costs to the County.
title: Request: Board review and determination of internet accessibility of use of the County Website for legal notices pursuant to Florida Statute §50.0311 - Lynsey Darragh, ASD

description:
Recommendation: We recommend awarding Parts A and B of the project to Extreme Land Restoration, LLC of Lynn Haven, Florida, for a total amount of $4,211,077.09, contingent upon agency approval, for the western 9,300 feet of Pooser Road.
Background: This project is funded 100% through the Florida Commerce Job Growth Grant Fund, with a total project budget of $4,680,059.00, of which approximately $4,230,000.00 is available for construction.
On July 31st, the County received five highly competitive bids for the project. Extreme Land Restoration submitted the lowest bid at $4,981,434.59, covering the paving of the full 2.3-mile length of Pooser Road. (See attached bid tabulation.)
After extensive efforts by County staff to obtain necessary easements, it was determined that paving could not be completed along the eastern 2,500 feet due to lack of willingness to provide the necessary easements. Consequently, the project was redesigned to focus on the western 9,300 feet, utilizing existing County-owned right-of-way to allow construction to proceed. This modification and the resulting reduction in project length have been reflected in the recommended award amount. (See attached unit price breakdown.)
The contract also includes reimbursement to the City of Marianna for culvert installation at the Pooser Road and Kynesville Highway intersection. Also included in the contract, the contractor will assist the City’s grant-funded work for construction of the FDOT-required turn lanes and traffic signal at the same intersection. Funding for these improvements will be shared between the City and County, with Marianna contributing $670,579.56 and the County contributing $232,618.36, all from grant funds.
title: Request: Board approval to Award RB-2425-02 Pooser Road Construction to Extreme Land Restoration, LLC - David Melvin, Melvin Engineering

description:
The Road & Bridge Department currently has 15 motor graders on lease from Caterpillar. 5 of the motor graders will expire February 5, 2026. Staff's plan for purchasing to replace those is to utilize the Florida Local Governance Finance Program (FLGFC) and buy resulting in Jackson County ownership, rather than lease them. Owning them will provide us with flexibility when it comes to follow-on purchases and the ability to surplus the motor graders when most appropriate. The FLGFC Program is a variable interest rate program. The county has previously used this program in 2018 to borrow 2 million dollars to perform work on the County Jail, Ag Center Roof, and Fire & Dispatch construction.
The resolution provides a total of $5 million to give the county the option to draw down additional money to purchase and replace the motor graders that have leases expiring in 2027. The county would only draw down the initial $1,650,000 to purchase 5 motor graders for deployment in February 2026.
Alternate option for financing:
Komatsu Financing – $1,482,408. 60 months @ $4,941.36 per machine per month
Includes maintenance plan
Residual for each machine to purchase at end of lease is $95,323.32 per vehicle
Staff recommended option for financing:
FAC Financing – $1,650,000. 60 months @ ~$6000 per machine per month
Includes maintenance plan
The County would own the machine out right, and no additional costs would apply for hours on the machine.
title: Request: Board discussion and approval of Resolution to loan funds from FAC/FLGFC - Tyler Schaeffer, Procurement Officer

description:
The requirements of Senate Bill 784, amending Sections 177.091 and 177.111 Florida Statutes were enacted effective July 1, 2025, requiring changes to the subdivision platting process of the County. The bill requires local governments to review, process, and approve plat or replat submittals without action or approval by the governing body through an administrative authority and an official designated by ordinance or resolution. The administrative authority must be a department, division, or other agency of the local government, and include an administrative officer or employee.
Under the bill, the authority must provide written notice in response to a submittal within seven days acknowledging receipt, identifying any missing documents or information required, and providing information regarding the approval process including requirements and timeframes.
Unless the applicant requests an extension, the authority must approve, approve with conditions, or deny the submittal within the timeframe identified in the initial written notice. A denial must be accompanied by an explanation of why the submittal was denied, specifically citing unmet requirements.
A SPECIAL EXCEPTION OR A VARIANCE TO THE DEVELOPMENT REGULATIONS WILL REQUIRE APPROVAL FROM THE COUNTY REGULATORY BOARDS IN ADDITION TO THE PLAT PROCESS.
title:
Request: Second Reading and Adoption of Changes to the Subdivision Ordinance -
Kim Cole Sweazy, Community Development Director

description:
Requested Action:Approve entering into a managed services contract with Mobile Communications of the Americas (MCA) for the support, maintenance, and lifecycle management of public safety radios and associated equipment on radio towers in Jackson County. The annual contract amount is $58,507.50, to be funded by the local law “Automation” fund.
Background & Justification:
Public safety radios are a mission-critical component of Jackson County’s emergency communications system, used daily by law enforcement, fire, EMS, and other first responders. This radio equipment serves as the lifeline between the field and the Jackson County Sheriff's Office Emergency Communications Center, and any downtime directly affects responder safety and service to the public.
Currently, Jackson County contracts with managed service providers for all other critical components of the emergency 911 system, including CAD (Computer-Aided Dispatch), 911 call handling systems, and dispatch radio consoles. The radio system, however, remains the only core public safety communications infrastructure not supported under a comprehensive managed services agreement.
By contracting with MCA for managed services, Jackson County will be provided the following services and benefits:
Daily checks of infrastructure via remote management tools.
Perform system management duties via a Radio Management solution, including managing system and subscriber configurations and changing IDs and aliases.
Provide remote dispatch telephone support as needed to the dispatch center.
Maintain Excel document of County subscriber inventory as related to subscriber units on the system by the respective County entity.
Ensure proactive monitoring, preventative annual maintenance, and priority response for all radios and related equipment.
Reduce downtime and extend the life of equipment through routine servicing and firmware/software updates.
Ensure system reliability and operational continuity across all participating public safety agencies in the County.
This managed services contract is essential to maintaining parity with the level of support already in place for other critical communications systems and to provide first responders with reliable equipment they depend on for their safety and for protecting the citizens of Jackson County.
Fiscal Impact:
The total annual contract amount is $58,507.50, to be paid from the local law “Automation” fund. No additional general fund dollars are requested.
title: Request: Board Approval of Managed Services Contract for Public Safety Radios and Equipment - Daniel Warren, Director of Communications

description:
On June 12, 2025, Jackson County issued an Invitation to Bid to solicit sealed bids for the Endeavor Museum Shell and Structural Repairs project. Bids for this project were received from two (2) construction contractors and were opened on Tuesday, July 15, 2025.
The lowest responsive bidder for the project was Monolith Construction with a total bid price of $1,136,994.12. This bid price is substantially over the project’s remaining construction budget which is currently at $808,410.00. This budget figure is comprised of $500,000 in Grant Funds and $328,584.12 in previously committed County TDC matching Funds. The resulting difference of the low bid compared to the project budget is $328,584.12.
At the County’s July 22 meeting, the board authorized Melvin Engineering to conduct value engineering negotiations with the low-bid contractor to bring the project within budget. Negotiations have since been completed in accordance with the Value Engineering Summary. It is opinion of Melvin Engineering that the reduced project scope still accomplishes the overall intent and objective of the initial project and will allow the county to complete additional renovation activities as future funding becomes available. Approximately $38,580 in additional funds will be provided by the TDC for associated design costs that are not eligible within the grant.
Recommended award amount is $808,410.00.
title: Request: Board approval to award 2425-20 Endeavor Museum Shell Reconstruction and Structural Repairs to Monolith Construction - Lucas Mayo, Grants/Contracts Manager

attachments.name: National Black Growers Council Farm Field Day Proclamation

description: The National Black Growers Council (NBGC) will host its 2025 Model Farm Field Day in Jackson County, Florida, on Friday, September 12, 2025, at Gilbert Farms, located at 5275 Old US Road in Marianna. The event will be hosted by Dexter Gilbert, a third-generation farmer, and will highlight cotton and peanut production through innovative practices and on-farm demonstrations. The Model Farm Field Day is designed to bring together farmers, agricultural professionals, and community members to showcase advancements in row crop production that improve efficiency, sustainability, and profitability. This year’s program will feature demonstrations including FloRun 52N Peanuts with 100% No-Till Planting, Broadcasting Cover Crops Before Peanut Harvest, Drone Cotton Defoliation vs. Ground Application, Drone Seeding Cover Crops Ahead of Cotton Harvest, and a Cotton Stalk Puller & Round Roll Cotton Harvest demonstration. The proclamation presented for adoption recognizes the significance of this event and its role in supporting the agricultural industry, community engagement, and innovation within Jackson County.

description:
The Jackson County EDC is requesting final approval and full support from both Jackson County and the City of Marianna for a property deal involving approximately 235 acres of jointly owned land. The land is located at Distribution Park (Exit 136 - I10) and consists of three parcels:75 acres (Parcel ID 17-4N-10-0000-0030-0060)
80 acres (Parcel ID 19-4N-10-0000-0020-0010)
80 acres (a portion of Parcel ID 18-4N-10-0000-0010-0030)
The buyer, TPA Group, has expressed interest in purchasing the land for manufacturing, technology, or distribution purposes. The agreement grants TPA Group an exclusive option to purchase the land in phases, with an initial payment of $23,500 that will apply toward the purchase price of the property.
Key details of the agreement include:Option Period: 12 months, with the possibility of two 12-month extensions.
Option Price: $100 per acre, non-refundable, except in case of default by the seller.
Purchase Price: $10,000 per acre upon exercising the option.
Extension of Option: The buyer can extend the option period by paying an extension fee and providing documentation of their costs related to the property.
Additionally, TPA Group will work with the City of Marianna and Jackson County to obtain necessary approvals and permits for the development of the land, including any required zoning changes, utility access, and permits. They also plan to apply for grants to support infrastructure development.
The EDC is seeking the final approval of the Jackson County Board of County Commissioners and the City of Marianna to proceed with the sale and development of this property.

The legislation requires local governments to designate a specific administrative authority (including, but not limited to, county administrator, deputy county administrator, or other high-ranking county department or division director with direct or indirect oversight responsibility for the county's land development, housing, utilities, or public works program) to receive and process all plat and re-plat applications and to approve, approve with conditions, or deny the submittal within an identified timeframe. The requirement applies to any subdivision plat that is in compliance with F.S. 177.091 (Plats Made For Recording) and mandates that the local government process and approve plats and re-plats through administrative staff only without requiring public hearings and votes.

description:
The current One Cent Sales Tax Ordinance (2009-05) sunsets on December 31, 2025. By Ordinance, proceeds for this tax revenue must be deposited into Transportation Trust for operating the Road and Bridge Department. These proceeds fund a significant portion (approximately 50%) of the Transportation Trust Fund.
In the current budget year (2024-25), the County is projected to receive approximately $5.8 million dollars from the One Cent Tax. In addition to this amount, the Transportation Trust Fund is subsidized by General Revenue by $5.8 million.
The Board tabled the matter at the June 10, 2025 meeting, and directed the County Attorney and Staff to gather further information.
The Board voted at the July 8, 2025 meeting to set the public hearing for this matter.
Providing that the funds are not used for bonds, and will not be approved by referendum, we are not required to complete a performance audit for the Office of Program Analysis and Government Accountability with the Florida Department of Revenue.
title: Request: Board adoption of the one-cent sales tax ordinance - Lynsey Darragh, ASD

description:
The current One Cent Sales Tax Ordinance (2009-05) sunsets on December 31, 2025. By Ordinance, proceeds for this tax revenue must be deposited into Transportation Trust for operating the Road and Bridge Department. These proceeds fund a significant portion (approximately 50%) of the Transportation Trust Fund.
In the current budget year (2024-25), the County is projected to receive approximately $5.8 million dollars from the One Cent Tax. In addition to this amount, the Transportation Trust Fund is subsidized by General Revenue by $5.8 million.
The Board tabled the matter at the June 10, 2025 meeting, and directed the County Attorney and Staff to gather further information.
Providing that the funds are not used for bonds, and will not be approved by referendum, we are not required to complete a performance audit for the Office of Program Analysis and Government Accountability with the Florida Department of Revenue.
Staff requests that we set the public hearing on July 22, 2025 at 9:00 am to adopt the ordinance.
title: Request: Board approval to set a public hearing for the one-cent sales tax ordinance - Lynsey Darragh, ASD

description:
Jackson County has been selected by the State of Florida to be a CORE Funding County for the upcoming year. The Coordinated Opioid Recovery (C.O.R.E.) project begins July 1 and the money will be distributed by the Northwest FL Health Network. The county is set to receive an approximate $700,000.00 the first year. The CORE project is made up of three main components: rescue response (EMS), stabilization/assessment (Hospital), and receiving clinics for MAT Therapy and Treatment for OUD and SUD along with recovery supports. The Law Enforcement portion of CORE project will become available for State Fiscal Year 26-27 (Next Year).
Attached is the scope of work of our 24/7 MAT provider for the CORE Project, PanCare Health. The cost for the first year is $500,000.00 for their services.
For the remaining $200,000.00, staff are recommending a plan to fund additional fire-rescue paramedic and EMT positions to provide a 12-hour additional ambulance in service seven days a week to respond to the increase in call volume. The plan includes creating two paramedic and two EMT full-time positions that will work alternating 12-hour shifts to provide coverage during peak times. If approved by the board, this plan will be submitted to the NWF Health Network for their approval. The addition of EMTs and Paramedics for response is an approved use of CORE funding as outlined by the staff at NWF Health Network. The positions will be partly funded out of the CORE Project funding and the remaining balance will be funded by the anticipated Public Emergency Medical Transportation Program funds that are returned to the County.
title: Request: Board discussion and approval of the Coordinated Opioid Recovery (C.O.R.E.) Project Plan Funding - Lynsey Darragh, ASD

description:
The current One Cent Sales Tax Ordinance (2009-05) sunsets on December 31, 2025. By Ordinance, proceeds for this tax revenue must be deposited into Transportation Trust for operating the Road and Bridge Department. These proceeds fund a significant portion (approximately 50%) of the Transportation Trust Fund.
In the current budget year (2024-25), the County is projected to receive approximately $5.8 million dollars from the One Cent Tax. In addition to this amount, the Transportation Trust Fund is subsidized by General Revenue by $5.8 million.
The Board indicated at the February 24, 2025 meeting that the funds from the new Ordinance should continue to go into the Transportation Trust. If there is a modification that no longer restricts these funds to Transportation Trust, the County will be required to have a performance audit completed before the new Ordinance takes effect.
Staff requests that we set the public hearing on July 8, 2025 at 9:00 am to adopt the ordinance.
title: Request: Board approval to set a public hearing for the one-cent sales tax ordinance - Lynsey Darragh, ASD

description:
The Jackson County Planning Commission serves as an advisory and recommending entity to the Board of County Commissioners as required by F.S. Ch 163. The Planning Commission is tasked with holding a public hearing on all proposed development applications that require a public hearing before the Board of County Commissioners, prior to the BOCC decision.
The Planning Commission has many review responsibilities including:
(1) Conduct the Comprehensive Planning program and prepare the Comprehensive Plan or elements or portions thereof for the County.
(2) Coordinate such Comprehensive Plan or elements or portions thereof with the Comprehensive Plans of other appropriate local governments and the State.
(3) Recommend such Comprehensive Plan or elements or portions thereof to the Board of County Commissioners for adoption; and
(4) Monitor and oversee the effectiveness and status of the Comprehensive Plan and recommend to the Board of County Commissioners such changes in the Comprehensive Plan as may be required from time to time.
The County Planning Commission, as the local planning agency, shall consist of seven members, each of whom shall be appointed by a majority vote of the Board of County Commissioners. Members shall serve a term of three years.
One of the two At Large positions on the Commission was vacated at the end of 2024 by Tyler Lipford who served from 2018-2024. The vacancy was advertised in the Jackson County Times, on the County Vacancy webpage, and on the JCBOCC Facebook page for two weeks closing February 8, 2025. Four applications were received to fill the vacant At Large position on the Planning Commission.
As the Department responsible for requesting appointments to the Planning Commission, we are asking for direction on how to move forward in presenting the multiple applications to the Board for appointment.
Below I have listed the current representatives serving as volunteers on the Planning Commission as well as information on the four applicants for the remaining vacant seat on the Commission.

description:
The current One Cent Sales Tax Ordinance (2009-05) sunsets on December 31, 2025. By Ordinance, proceeds for this tax revenue must be deposited into Transportation Trust for operating the Road and Bridge Department. These proceeds fund a significant portion (approximately 50%) of the Transportation Trust Fund. In order to renew this Ordinance, the Board will need to determine if the funds for the new Ordinance should continue to go into Transportation Trust or in General Revenue.
In the current budget year (2024-25), the County is projected to receive approximately $5.8 million dollars from the One Cent Tax. In addition to this amount, the Transportation Trust Fund is subsidized by General Revenue by $5.8 million.
If there is a modification that no longer restricts these funds to Transportation Trust, the County will be required to have a performance audit completed before the new Ordinance takes effect.
title: Request: Board discussion of One Cent Tax Ordinance - Sarah Sun, HR Director

description:

If they leave the agency for any reason, the monies contributed by the Board are due back to the County.
Mr. Wiggins has accepted employment with another agency before the end of his 36 month term. The Board paid a total of $9,033 towards the cost of tuition and the educational stipend. He is requesting that he be allowed to make payments over 18 months in the amount of $501.83. Payments will start March 1,2025, and be due no later than the 15th day of each month thereafter.

description:
A code violation case was opened in March 2024 citing Duty of Maintenance at 976 Daniel Drive owned by Michael Rhodes. The violation was not remedied by the April 5, 2024, deadline and was heard at the April Magistrate Hearing with an order to remedy the violation by June 4, 2024, with fines of $50/day until compliance. The property was reinspected August 12, 2024, with continued violation. A Fines and Fees assessment was sent to Mr. Rhodes on September 3, 2024; the assessed fines of $6,450.00 were paid through a closing agent on September 11, 2024.
On November 20, 2024, Mr. Rhodes contacted Code Enforcement officer, Jay Clark, and provided evidence that he had been granted additional time by the prior Code Enforcement Officer to July 2, 2024, and Mr. Rhodes requested refund of the paid fines. A discussion between the Code Enforcement Officer, Community Development Director, and County Administrator determined that a refund of $4,400.00 could be justified based on evidence of miscommunication between the Code Enforcement officer and Mr. Rhodes. The fines were recalculated by Code Enforcement for a noncompliance period from July 2, 2024, and August 12, 2024, when the property was determined to be in compliance for a new fine of $2,050.00.
title: Request: Board authorization for a partial refund of Code Enforcement fines to Michael Rhodes, 976 Daniel Dr, Alford - Jay Clark, Code Enforcement Officer

description:
On September 24th, 2024, the JCBOCC voted to have Road and Bridge sell and install driveway culverts. County ordinance 44-57, "Construction, alteration and impact costs to be borne by applicant" already provides direction for this process. Michelle Jordan explained, "under state law, if the BOCC adopts a rule or policy by ordinance, it can only be amended by ordinance". We believe rescinding the 9/24 vote and maintaining ordinance 44-57 as is, is the best course of action.
Since we do not charge application or inspection fees, like some other counties, the applicant is already seeing a cost savings. As a reminder, five of the counties researched make the property owner responsible for the installation. Additionally, selling culverts from Road and Bridge's inventory will take business away from local vendors. It should also be noted that we will need to charge sales tax if we sell the culverts.
In 2023 there were just over 80 permits issued requiring culverts. While actual costs vary greatly, the average cost to install a culvert is $1,325 for labor, equipment, and dirt/rock, with a combined average of over 11 employee hours per install. Using the 2023 permits, that translates to around $106,000 and 880 employee hours per year.
The primary issue we had with the owner being responsible for the installation was the lack of guidance. We would like to correct this by providing a design standard similar to FDOT. Because our rights-of-way vary so much, we believe it is best to consult with an engineer.
We also need direction on how to proceed with permit applications received on or after September 24th.
title: TABLED Request: Board discussion of 9/24/24 motion for Road and Bridge to sell and install culverts - Jeffrey Register, Road and Bridge Director

description:
DHM was tasked with developing a comprehensive assessment of the proposed Jackson County Magnolia Boat Landing development project via a Feasibility Study. The study aims to provide a clear understanding of its feasibility and potential impact on the environment along with recommended construction improvement options. The site’s layout and design considerations have been analyzed to optimize space utilization, enhance accessibility, and promote efficient land use.
As part of the drafting of the final plan document public input on the proposed design was received via a public hearing held on 11/16/2026 and now is being presented to the board of commissioners for their review and comment.
1. Improve the condition and functionality of the existing boat ramp through rehabilitation or replacement of deteriorated concrete infrastructure.
2. Increase available parking capacity.
3. Improve pedestrian safety by providing designated walkways and additional traffic routes
4. Enhance accessibility through appropriately designed parking spaces, accessible routes, and supporting facilities.
5. Address existing shoreline erosion and drainage concerns to protect the boat ramp and adjacent recreational areas.
6. Improve the overall user experience through additional informational signage, lighting, and restroom accessibility.
7. Preserve the natural character of the site while minimizing potential environmental impacts associated with construction activities.
title: Report: Board update of Magnolia Landing Feasibility Study and Preliminary Site Plan - Lucas Mayo, Grants/Contracts Manager
